option_relations.rationale: The option directly matches the label of the leaf ID FLAT.1, indicating a direct equivalence in diagnosis.
Gastric outlet obstruction is considered but does not directly relate to the specific diagnosis of Superior mesenteric artery syndrome.
Peptic stricture of the stomach is an alternative cause and does not directly relate to the diagnosis of Superior mesenteric artery syndrome.
Neoplasm of the stomach is considered as an alternative cause and does not directly relate to the diagnosis of Superior mesenteric artery syndrome.
Annular pancreas, diabetic gastroparesis, internal hernia, and duodenal bezoar are alternative causes and do not directly relate to the diagnosis of Superior mesenteric artery syndrome.
Peptic ulcer disease and duodenal tumors are considered among other causes of obstruction and were excluded, not directly relating to the diagnosis of Superior mesenteric artery syndrome.
Scleroderma and other collagen or vascular disorders are considered as mimics but do not directly relate to the diagnosis of Superior mesenteric artery syndrome.
Vascular compression due to a reduced aortomesenteric angle supports the diagnosis of Superior mesenteric artery syndrome, indicating a subtype or specific instance of the condition.
